{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that auditory flankers would facilitate the processing of visual targets when their letter names are identical (perceptual-congruent) and that they would also speed up late processing stages when auditory flankers and targets match the same response (response-congruent).",
  "design": "within",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Three congruency conditions: perceptual-congruent (target and flanker identical), response-congruent (target and flanker different but mapped to the same response), and incongruent (target and flanker mapped to different responses).",
  "outcome_measure": "Reaction time (RT) and percentage of correct responses (PC).",
  "population_and_setting": "36 participants recruited from the University of Tübingen, tested in a noise-shielded cabin.",
  "sample_size_total": 36,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "University students receiving course credits.",
  "analysis_plan": "One-way ANOVAs with conditions (perceptual-congruent, response-congruent, incongruent) performed separately for PC and RT.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The visual target always appeared 500 ms after the onset of the auditory flanker. Two letters were assigned to one response and the remaining two to the other. Trials with RTs outside 150-1500 ms were excluded."
}
